record.original_question: Let (u_i)_{i >= 1} be a strictly increasing sequence of integers greater than 1. Construct a sieve by, at step i, keeping one number among the next u_i - 1 remaining numbers and deleting every u_i-th remaining number. What relationship between the generator sequence (u_i) and the resulting remaining sequence can be proved?

evidence.quote: Problem: study the relationship between sequence ui, i = 1, 2, 3, ..., and the remaining sequence resulted from the general sieve.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(u_i)_{i\geq 1}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of integers with $u_i > 1$ for all $i$. Define a sieve on the positive integers $1,2,3,\dots$ as follows. At step $i=1,2,3,\dots$, consider the current sequence of remaining integers (with step $0$ being the full sequence of positive integers). Partition the remaining integers, starting from the first one not yet processed, into consecutive blocks of length $u_i$; in each such block, keep the first $u_i - 1$ entries and delete the $u_i$-th entry. After performing this step for every $i\geq 1$, let $R = (r_1 < r_2 < \cdots)$ denote the sequence of integers that are never deleted.

Establish a precise relationship between the generator sequence $(u_i)$ and the resulting surviving sequence $R$. In particular, derive formulas, recursions, asymptotic density estimates, or analytic/combinatorial identities that express properties of $R$ (such as its counting function, asymptotic density, or generating function) in terms of the sequence $(u_i)$.

(Note: the classical case $u_i = $ the $i$-th surviving integer greater than $1$ recovers a self-referential sieve in the spirit of the lucky-number sieve; here $(u_i)$ is an arbitrary prescribed strictly increasing sequence.)
artifact.status_search_result: The question asks for a general theory relating an arbitrary generator sequence to the sequence surviving its position-based sieve, generalizing the lucky-number sieve. No general structural theorem of this form appears in the literature; existing work (Wikipedia on lucky numbers; Briggs's generalizations; recent arXiv work on lucky numbers, 2025) treats specific cases and asymptotic densities rather than providing a general relationship for arbitrary $(u_i)$. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lucky number - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Lucky numbers are generated by a sieve similar to the Sieve of Eratosthenes that eliminates numbers based on their position in the remaining set.
status_evidence.claim: The classical position-based sieve yielding lucky numbers is well known, but the general-sequence variant is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: On the Fundamental Arithmetical Structure and Distribution of Lucky Numbers
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) study of arithmetical structure and distribution of lucky numbers.
status_evidence.claim: Recent research focuses on the classical lucky sieve, not on a general theory for arbitrary generator sequences.
